# Deck3 Chapter 1 Comparative Design Lessons — 2026-10-09

**Status:** Presentation-design feedback; not scientific authority, a completed thesis result, or approval of any existing slide baseline.

## Reviewed variants
- **ASU Professional text-only (16/16):** strongest slide headline/typography, full thermal-study source mix, precise directional qualification, readable reference groups; no diagrams by design.
- **Expert Deck3 assembled (16/16, 11/11 figures):** original restrained two-system / two independent heat lanes / evidence-gated pathways; figures often too small and scientific source list too general to substantiate the particular proposed heat mechanisms.
- **Dossiya provisional assembled (16/16, 10/11 figures):** detailed evidence/AC-interface graphics, case-specific source context and explanatory icons; too many miniature annotations/arrowheads, missing slide-13 image, not releasable as a completed 11-figure deck.
- Compare wording independently of illustration. Do not silently replace any already approved source copy when learning from these variants.

## Permanent user-directed visible-copy rule

**Never print metadata labels in native slide shapes or inside graphics.** Specifically reject literal **MAIN MESSAGE**, **THREE KEY POINTS**, **MAIN IDEA**, **3 BULLETS**, and similar template/authoring labels. The actual scientific main statement and substantive supporting content must remain visible, with its source/citations and native editability preserved.

- The manifest may keep a `message` field and three `bullets` for structural discipline: these are **internal authoring metadata**, not audience language.
- Introduce the scientific claim directly under the slide title. Show support as crisp native statements, a well-aligned evidence table, or evidence-bearing infographic rather than narrating the template.
- `General Objective`, `Specific Objectives`, `System Boundary`, `Evidence`, and `References` are permissible **meaningful content headings**; frozen GO/SO1–SO3 wording remains verbatim.
- Do not delete approved message or bullet content when removing the authoring labels; a new outline or shorter wording requires separate approval.

## Scientific corrections learned

1. Preserve independent P and **full** T_e system boundaries and a separately identified active case subset; list communication **and** control along with EVSE/RESS/vehicle/propulsion/auxiliaries/circuits/connection.
2. Common heat must produce **parallel external forcing lanes**, not a heat-induced cross-system arrow without independently verified mechanism.
3. Qualify P→T_e and T_e→P separately; candidate T_e→P must trace **grid-side AC input behavior**, not infer transformer response directly from DC charging-power output.
4. A charging-demand effect on Power System loading is not the same as reverse grid energy transfer. Label directions with actual transferred or affected quantity.
5. Thermal state, allowed capability, actual electrical flow, electricity/mobility service, resilience and sustainability are separate quantities/views.
6. Existing literature studies transformer heat effects and service disruption, and heat-related charger behavior for bounded equipment; do not claim all such coupling is first/new or validated for the eventual chosen case. Use source-specific adjacent citations for each externally supported fact.
7. Verification ≠ calibration ≠ independent validation; no validated thermal coefficients, curves, thresholds or observed service endpoints may be created by graphical inference.
8. Frozen objective slides may be text-led or use an approved separate companion visual. Do not shrink exact objective text into unreadable labels or repeat it wholesale in the graphic.
9. The working question wording and future contribution remain OPEN/proposed; numerical results and final case-specific novelty have not been established.

## Scientific figure dominance and visual quality

- Existing small right-side diagrams do **NOT** meet the user-directed target of **75% meaningful figure coverage of usable content area** (default allowable 70–80%). No full-deck 75% release claim until source geometry and measurable effective content occupancy are actually updated, rendered, and verified.
- Existing Expert figure rectangles on ordinary slides ~5.8×3.94 inches; provisional ~5.8×3.26 inches. Those occupy only roughly 45%/38% of a representative 12×4.2-inch content rectangle, **upper-bound image rectangles, not audited meaningful-science coverage**.
- Re-layout at Stage 1, not by enlarging a white padded figure at Stage 3. If immutable slide copy will not legibly fit in 20–30% residual usable area, block and request an approved split or record a documented textual/long-objectives exception.
- Keep all interiors and backgrounds white. Increase meaningful visual/label size, reduce repeated micro-labels/icons, reserve arrowheads for traceable relations, and make arrow semantics explicit in QA.
- Scientific PNG/SVG previews, file integrity and exact text/notes equality do **not** prove physical validation or adequate projection-scale typography.

## Acceptance regression checks for future Deck3

1. Visible text on **all** generated slides has no authoring-label tokens (`MAIN MESSAGE`, `THREE KEY POINTS`, ...).
2. Exact frozen objectives remain present and unaltered; references/citations and native editable slide content preserved.
3. Correct figure-to-slide matching; 11/11 required assets for this Chapter 1 deck, not 10/11.
4. On eligible newly re-laid-out slides, record U/V bounds and effective visual share; 0.70–0.80 pass band, no fake whitespace coverage. Mark legacy generator `NOT_VERIFIED_75_PERCENT` until geometry implementation and visual tests exist.
5. Render every slide and audit projected legibility, physical arrows, claims, boundary semantics, and figure clipping before release.

**Source basis:** user-provided Chapter 1 deck variants/contact sheets and the current canonical project authority. Design review is qualitative and is not an amendment of scientific thesis scope or the research objectives.
